messages:
Anika: Heads-up: starting 03:14 UTC we saw a thermal pulse on local NVMe in us-west1-b, iops saturation -> attach timeouts. GPU capacity drop ~28%.
Raj: logs? can you paste nvme and janitor stats?
Anika: paste: ```
nvme0n1: err_count=7, write_retries=9, temp_c=85
janitor: running=300, pending=1200, scrub_rate=0.9
attach-manager: attach_wait=12.4s, failures=42
```
infra-bot: Alert: storage-health (us-west1-b) triggered. Incident INC-2026-4721 created.
Liam: oncall - I'm in. Looks like concurrent scrubs + heavy training batch launches. Thermal spike correlates with scrub start times.
Sasha: Can we deprioritize scrubs on GPU-hosting racks and throttle janitor on region?
Marta: quick mitigation: set janitor.scratch_throttle=0.4 for us-west1, and reduce per-node scrub workers from 6->1.
Raj: Rolling feature flag now to us-west1-b. Pushing to 10% canary first.
Anika: Canary hosts show attach lat down from 18s -> 7s after throttle. Temperature started falling ~40s post-change.
Liam: Also flip scheduler to prefer cached-ephemeral pool to keep new attaches off hot drives.
Sasha: Will coordinate with capacity team to bump reserved overprovision for 30m window.
infra-bot: Flag changes applied by raj. Audit: curl -XPOST $FLAGS/api -d 'janitor.scratch_throttle=0.4; region=us-west1'
Marta: After immediate mitigation, we still need follow-ups: 1) thermal-aware scrubbing (rate limit by temp), 2) stagger scrub windows across AZs, 3) add per-node temp SLO in console, 4) add auto-evacuate for nodes hitting temp+reassigns.
Raj: Adding a short post-incident checklist to run: SMART histograms, scrub backlog distribution, and scheduler bias logs.
Anika: I'll open RFC for thermal-aware janitor and link dashboards.
Liam: Marking incident mitigated for now; keeping throttles for 45m then revert if stable.
Sasha: thanks team. Please leave runbook steps so oncall can act faster next time. :thumbsup:
Anika: copying runbook edits here and will link RFC once drafted.
